title: Canada’s Pembina Advances Gas-Fired Data Center Project
source_used: CBC News (EnergyNow, the pool item, returns HTTP 403 and its URL is dated July 2026)
key_facts: Pembina Pipeline, Morgan Stanley Infrastructure Partners and Kineticor Asset Management gave the go-ahead to the Greenlight Electricity Centre, a natural gas plant serving a data centre customer.

The project is expected to cost $4.6 billion; the 932-megawatt plant would be built in Sturgeon County north of Edmonton, with startup targeted for the second half of 2030, and permits would allow capacity to double.
The province and companies did not identify the data centre customer.
Alberta prioritises projects that bring their own power generation; Premier Danielle Smith said such a framework would reduce transmission costs on Alberta's utility bills.
The Pembina Institute, a clean-energy think tank unrelated to the company, called the plan a missed opportunity to use cheaper renewables.
quote_evidence: Pembina Pipeline Corp. and two partners have given the go-ahead to the Greenlight Electricity Centre, a natural gas plant serving a data centre customer.
The province and companies did not identify the data centre customer they're serving.
